result: At exact rmcp-v3.1.4 release source, TaskManager::update_task and TaskManager::cancel_task apply by task_id with no generation/version/attempt/request-identity/current-status CAS precondition. update_task removes and delivers any currently pending response whose key matches; unknown/already-answered/superseded keys are ignored and duplicates after the first delivery are therefore harmless, but a stale response that still names a currently pending key is not rejected by any historical fence. cancel_task sets cancel_requested and signals cooperative cancellation for any existing task_id; terminal tasks keep their terminal payload, but running tasks can be affected without a generation/version fence. TTL expiry can make a task unknown, which is a lifetime check rather than historical concurrency protection.
